input.query: Give me a forecast: will Sweden's opposition centre-left bloc win a majority of the Riksdag's seats in the 13 September 2026 general election?

sources.title: Sweden's campaign opens
sources.text:
Sweden's general election is set for 13 September 2026.
The incumbent three-party centre-right coalition has governed since 2022.
The opposition centre-left bloc campaigns as a joint list of four parties.
Public broadcasting hosts the leaders' debates in the final month.
sources.author: Elsa Nyberg

sources.title: Opinion polls show a close race
sources.text:
Poll aggregates through late summer put the two blocs within a few points.
Neither bloc has held a double-digit lead at any point this year.
Turnout in Swedish elections has exceeded 84 percent in recent cycles.

sources.title: Budget disputes strain the coalition
sources.text:
The governing coalition's autumn budget talks exposed disputes over energy prices.
One coalition partner has publicly questioned a flagship tax pledge.
The Social Democrats campaign on welfare and energy prices.
sources.author: Johan Lindqvist

output.outcome: Sweden's centre-left bloc won a one-seat majority (175-176 of 349) in the 13 September 2026 general election, ousting the centre-right coalition led by Ulf Kristersson; Magdalena Andersson is set to return as prime minister. Only about 26,000 votes separated the blocs.
output.answer:
The council leans towards a change of government in Sweden. The campaign's frame ([Sweden's campaign opens](https://pre-event.example/sweden-campaign)) and the poll aggregate ([Opinion polls show a close race](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls)) suggest the centre-right's advantage is gone.

## Claim 1: Sweden's opposition centre-left bloc wins a majority of the Riksdag's 349 seats in the 13 September 2026 general election.
By 15 October 2026. Council verdict: **ACCEPTED**

Members weigh the tight polls ([Opinion polls show a close race](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls)) against the coalition's budget disputes ([Budget disputes strain the coalition](https://pre-event.example/sweden-budget)).

## Claim 2: Sweden's post-election government formation concludes before 1 November 2026.
By 1 November 2026. Council verdict: **UNRESOLVED**

Formation timelines rest on the seat count the election produces; the sources say little ([Sweden's campaign opens](https://pre-event.example/sweden-campaign)).

- Member 2: for — Strained budgets and joint campaigning point left. ([Source 3](https://pre-event.example/sweden-budget))
- Member 3: for — The incumbent's energy disputes cost votes. ([Source 3](https://pre-event.example/sweden-budget))
- Member 4: against — Incumbents rarely lose on one budget. ([Source 2](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls))
- Member 5: unsure — Within the margin of error. ([Source 2](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls))
- Member 6: for — High turnout favours challenger blocs. ([Source 2](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls))
- Member 7: for — The joint list's discipline beats coalition infighting. ([Source 1](https://pre-event.example/sweden-campaign), [Source 3](https://pre-event.example/sweden-budget))

### Claim 2: UNRESOLVED
2 of 7 voted for, 1 against, 4 unsure.

- Member 1: unsure — Formation timelines vary.
- Member 2: for — A one-seat margin still means a quick deal. ([Source 2](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls))
- Member 3: unsure — No basis.
- Member 4: unsure — Thin.
- Member 5: unsure — No lean.
- Member 6: for — Sweden forms governments fast. ([Source 2](https://pre-event.example/sweden-polls))
- Member 7: unsure — Too thin.

input.query: Give me a forecast: will Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign a joint defence agreement by 30 September 2026?

sources.title: A trilateral meeting is prepared
sources.text:
The three capitals announced a joint defence summit.
A bilateral defence pact between two of them already exists.
Their foreign ministers met earlier this year on joint security.
sources.author: Yusuf Demir

sources.title: The war's pressure grows
sources.text:
Missile fire has reached the gulf's oil exporters.
Regional states say security can no longer depend on outside powers.
Analysts expect closer defence ties among the four main states.
sources.author: Leyla Karim

sources.title: What the draft is said to say
sources.text:
The draft is described as a mutual-defence pledge without troop commitments.
Officials call it purely defensive in briefings.
A signing is expected at the summit itself.

output.outcome: On 7 August 2026 Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in Mecca, stipulating that an armed attack on any one of the three is an attack on all; Turkey's foreign minister called it technically the same as NATO's Article 5.
output.answer:
The council expects the trilateral defence pact to be signed. The announced summit ([A trilateral meeting is prepared](https://pre-event.example/mecca-prep)) and the war's pressure ([The war's pressure grows](https://pre-event.example/mecca-pressure)) make it near-certain; the text is expected to stay declaratory.
